high.title: TSMC Spends 100 Billion for Central Taiwan Science Park Major Upgrade, 15A Fab Mature Process to Convert to 4nm
high.summary: TSMC is launching a massive 100+ billion TWD upgrade plan for its Central Taiwan Science Park facilities. The 15A fab, currently operating 28-22nm mature processes, will be upgraded to 4nm advanced process technology. This involves relocating existing equipment to TSMC's Germany facility and installing new 4nm production equipment. The upgrade is part of TSMC's broader advanced process expansion strategy, alongside the ongoing construction of a 1.4nm fab in the Central Taiwan Science Park Phase II. The investment includes cleanroom facilities and advanced manufacturing equipment. This upgrade significantly enhances Taiwan's advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity and supports NVIDIA AI chip supply requirements. The move also triggers expansion plans for packaging partners like ASE Group, which is aggressively expanding capacity in central Taiwan through multiple facility acquisitions worth over 32 billion TWD in recent months.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Index Breaks 40,000 Points Setting 10 New Records, Analysts Call for Bullish Strategy with Potential to Challenge 41,200 Points This Week
high.summary: Taiwan's stock market shattered the "May weakness" myth with a spectacular performance, breaking 10 historical records in a single day. Key milestones include: largest intraday gain (1,828 points), largest closing gain (1,778 points), first close above 40,000 points, Taiwan Index Futures hitting 41,031 points, and electronics/semiconductor indices reaching new highs. The total market capitalization reached 143.56 trillion TWD. Foreign investors bought a net 669.75 billion TWD, marking the sixth-largest single-day purchase in history, with TSMC receiving 204.83 billion TWD in foreign buying. Major investment advisory firms remain bullish, expecting the index to challenge 41,200 points this week. They emphasize that current AI trends remain in early stages with no signs of deceleration, supported by US cloud service providers' capital expenditure potentially reaching 1.1-1.2 trillion USD next year. However, analysts warn of potential short-term volatility due to technical overbought conditions and advise monitoring key support levels.

medium.title: MediaTek Benefits from Robot Revolution as Jensen Huang Signals 1-3 Year Mainstream Adoption Timeline
medium.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang stated that reasoning-capable robots will become mainstream within 1-3 years, highlighting motors, hand components, and mechatronics as key areas. Analysts expect Hon Hai Group companies including Hon Hai (2317), Qisda (2328), and Foxconn Technology (2354) to benefit significantly from this robot revolution, with Qisda's European axial motor acquisition positioning it as a key player in Hon Hai's robot strategy.

medium.title: Five Major CSPs to Invest Over $1 Trillion Next Year, Boosting Orders for Quanta, Wistron
medium.summary: Morgan Stanley estimates that North America's five major cloud service providers will spend over $800 billion in capex this year, rising to $1.1 trillion in 2027 - the first time exceeding $1 trillion. This AI arms race intensification benefits ODM manufacturers like Hon Hai, Quanta, and Wistron. The spending represents nearly double 2025 levels and triple 2024 amounts, contributing approximately 2.5% to GDP growth this year and over 3% next year.

medium.title: Stock Queen Ardentec Q1 EPS Reaches 19.54 TWD with Strong Order Book Supporting Sequential Growth
medium.summary: Ardentec (6515) reported record Q1 net profit of 700 million TWD and EPS of 19.54 TWD, driven by strong AI and HPC demand for high-end test interfaces. Revenue reached 2.98 billion TWD, up 33.5% QoQ. The company is aggressively expanding pin production capacity from 3.5 million monthly to 6 million by Q2 and 8 million by year-end to meet surging demand.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Opens Over 14.2 Million Accounts with 61% Penetration Rate, Approaching Universal Stock Ownership
medium.summary: Taiwan's stock market reached 14.2 million accounts in April, representing 61% of the population - a new milestone toward "universal stock ownership." The fastest-growing demographic is 0-19 years old with 3.6% monthly growth, indicating parents' active long-term investment planning. The 20-30 age group added 29,000 accounts, showing strong participation from digital natives.

medium.title: Hon Hai Achieves Strongest April Revenue, Analysts Expect Sequential Growth Throughout Year
medium.summary: Hon Hai reported April revenue of 832 billion TWD, with first four months reaching 2.96 trillion TWD - both setting records for the same periods. Strong AI cloud product demand continues driving growth, with Q2 expected to outperform Q1. The second half will benefit from NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform and new iPhone 18 series, supporting the full-year sequential growth outlook.

medium.title: US Stocks Close with New Highs for Three Indices, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Surges Over 4% on AI Chip Fever
medium.summary: US markets rallied with S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index hitting record closing highs. The semiconductor index gained 4.23% to 10,980.58 points, bringing 2026 gains to 55%. AMD surged 14% after hours following strong datacenter revenue growth. Intel jumped 13% on reports of preliminary discussions with Apple for processor manufacturing. TSMC ADR gained 1% despite the broader semiconductor index decline the previous session.

medium.title: "AI Shrimp Farming" Trend Expands, Triggering NAND Memory Shortage to Benefit Phison, ADATA
medium.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI raised $5.5 billion combined to develop enterprise AI agents, driving exponential NAND demand. Phison CEO Pan notes enterprise AI agent training consumes "thousands of times" more NAND than consumer electronics. ADATA has built inventory exceeding 40 billion TWD, targeting 50 billion by June-end. The supply shortage is expected to persist as AI applications expand from data centers to edge computing.
